transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-12 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood CSM), Maya (Redwood SE), Priya (Synergy Head of MLOps), Tomás (Synergy VP Product), Leah (Security), Evan (Platform)

Agenda: Introductions, pilot success criteria, infrastructure choices, security + networking, next steps

00:00 Jordan: All right, everyone thanks for joining. Um quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan Patel, CSM, and Maya Chen is our SE. How about we go around real quick, list roles?
00:18 Priya: Hi this is Priya Rao, I run MLOps at Synergy, uh we'll own the pilot and the platform-side integration.
00:25 Tomás: Tomás Alvarez, VP Product, here to make sure feature parity and timelines map to product.
00:33 Leah: Leah Kim, Security Engineer, I'll be focused on compliance questions.
00:37 Evan: Evan Brooks, Platform Eng, I'll handle the network and kube bits on our end.
00:41 Maya: Awesome thanks, quick from our side--Maya Chen, Solutions Engineer, I'll run the tech and benchmarks with you.
00:47 Jordan: Great, agenda is to align success criteria for the pilot and pick a deployment path.

02:03 Jordan: Priya, can you start with high level goals for the pilot? What does success look like for Synergy?
02:12 Priya: Yeah sure. So primary metric is latency under load, we want p95 generation under 600 ms for our customer-facing flows. Also cost matters, we have a per-call budget target. Security is non-negotiable - no raw PHI leaves our VPC. So that means either private deployment or very strong isolation.
02:40 Tomás: And timeline - we aim to have an internal pilot in 6 weeks, production in about 3 months, assuming no major blockers.

04:01 Maya: Ok that's helpful. On the latency piece, we map that to model choice and deployment mode. Hosted is fastest to stand up but more of a black box for network. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and lower tail latency, Private (VPC) gives you the data residency/isolation you asked about. There's tradeoffs.
04:27 Priya: Right, we were thinking Dedicated could be a sweet spot - reserved GPUs but still managed. Leah, from security standpoint is Dedicated acceptable or do you want full VPC?
04:40 Leah: Dedicated is ok if we can get audit logs, KMS integration for key management, and guaranteed data retention policies. We also need SSO via SAML and RBAC for team access.

06:08 Jordan: We can provide SAML SSO and RBAC, and Redwood supports KMS-based encryption for keys. For audit logs, Maya will map what's available in the console and what we can stream to your SIEM.
06:26 Maya: Yes, we have per-route tracing and token-level cost visibility, and you can export logs to your Splunk/Datadog. There may be some field-name mismatches in the export — our logs call it "request_id" where your system may expect "trace_id" — we can show a sample.

07:10 Evan: Network question - for VPC peering, we'll need a list of CIDR blocks and expected egress ports. Also are we opening inbound ports or using outbound only?
07:25 Maya: Generally outbound from your VPC to ours on TLS egress. For private deployments it's inside your network so different. We'll send a network checklist.

08:40 Priya: About the PHI requirement - can we ensure persistent KV cache never stores PII?
08:47 Maya: Good call. Our KV cache can be configured to not persist specific fields, and we have token redaction in-flight. I'll include the config snippets.

09:32 Tomás: On the performance tests - can we run a scripted benchmark that mimics our 512-token median prompts? We're concerned about tokenization differences across models.
09:47 Maya: Absolutely. We'll run the benchmark on a model variant you pick. Suggest we start with a 7B quantized model and a larger 13B as fallbacks. We'll provide a spreadsheet with per-token latency and cost estimates.

11:15 Leah: SOC2 is a requirement for our vendors. Are you SOC2 Type II? Also audit windows and retention policies are important.
11:25 Jordan: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant. We can share the attestation and our security whitepaper, and Maya will walk through retention options — you can set retention to 90/180/365 days depending on package.

12:50 Priya: Who will own the production cutover? We'll need runbooks and a rollback plan if latency/regressions occur.
12:58 Jordan: CSM + your platform team should own that. We'll provide runbook templates and a canary rollout plan: start with 5% traffic, monitor latency and quality metrics, then ramp to 50% and 100%.

14:36 Evan: Could you explain how Redwood handles automatic fallback if capacity hits a limit? We need to avoid outages.
14:46 Maya: We have smart routing policies. If primary model variant is overloaded, requests can failover to cheaper/compatible variants or a lower-tier region. You can configure automatic fallback or strict fail to avoid mismatched outputs. There's a tradeoff: fallback keeps service up but might degrade quality.

16:02 Tomás: On cost — what's our monthly run estimate for the pilot? If we take 100k tokens a day with 2x growth, how does that look?
16:15 Maya: We'll model that in the spreadsheet but rough ballpark: quantized 7B can be ~0.5x the cost of a 13B; caching and batching reduce per-token cost significantly. We'll send scenarios.

18:00 Priya: Can we get token-level billing to our finance system? We need chargebacks per team.
18:07 Jordan: Yes, Redwood supports token-level cost breakdowns and per-route analytics. You can send billing exports or integrate via our API.

19:20 Leah: Encryption questions - where are keys stored if we use Redwood-managed KMS vs customer-managed?
19:28 Maya: With customer-managed KMS, keys remain in your cloud KMS and Redwood never sees unencrypted keys. With Redwood-managed KMS, we keep keys but with SOC2 controls. We'll document both flows.

21:03 Evan: For the pilot we'll likely want a small dedicated pool with autoscaling. Can you define the minimum node counts and expected cold start times?
21:15 Maya: Minimum is a 2-GPU pool for redundancy. Warm-up time depends on model size—quantized 7B is fast, warm start under 10s usually if KV warm, larger models 20-30s. We also support prewarming policies.

23:40 Priya: Rollback criteria — say p95 exceeds threshold by 20% or we see error rate bump — what's the threshold that triggers rollback?
23:52 Jordan: Typical thresholds are p95 > target + 25% or error rate > 1% sustained for 5 mins. We'll include recommended thresholds in the runbook but you can tune them.

25:30 Tomás: Regarding integration, will we use Redwood API directly from our backend or through a sidecar?
25:40 Maya: Both are supported. Many customers do a sidecar to centralize auth and caching. We'll share reference architecture for sidecar vs direct call patterns.

27:10 Leah: Audit trail — does Redwood provide immutable logs and tamper-evidence?
27:19 Maya: We can stream to your SIEM and maintain write-once storage for audit logs in the dedicated/private options. For hosted, log retention windows apply. We'll detail this.

29:05 Evan: About SSO - how long until we can finish SAML setup?
29:12 Jordan: Usually 2-3 business days for initial SAML config and testing. Then we'd do a staged access roll out.

31:00 Priya: For the pilot, we want to sample ~10k requests/day and ramp up. Can we set throttles and quotas per team?
31:10 Maya: Yes, Redwood supports quotas per token and per-route, plus rate limits. We'll include sample quota configs for your teams.

33:01 Tomás: Any risks we should flag now?
33:07 Maya: Model regression risk — we'll set up an eval suite to detect quality regressions tied to our prompt set. Also network misconfig and key management delays; those are common.

35:00 Priya: On the evals, can you run automated quality checks on a holdout set?
35:07 Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run evals and send alerts for regressions. We'll onboard your prompt/labels into the eval harness.

37:22 Leah: Can we see a sample of the security questionnaire responses? We have a vendor assessment doc.
37:29 Jordan: We'll attach the questionnaire answers and the SOC2 attestation in the follow-up email.

39:05 Evan: Network checklist / egress allowed ports - we'll need that to get firewall approvals.
39:12 Maya: We'll include a concise network checklist with CIDRs and port list. Note: TLS 443 outbound and a few control ports if using private link.

41:00 Tomás: Okay — what's the immediate next milestone?
41:06 Jordan: Deliverables within 3 business days: runbook, pilot checklist, benchmark plan, and proposed times for security deep-dive. Then your team to confirm network diagram and review pricing.

43:20 Priya: Who is our main SE contact for the benchmark runs?
43:25 Maya: That will be me, Maya. I'll coordinate the stress tests and share the spreadsheet.

45:10 Leah: Last thing — retention policy on logs for PHI must be explicit. We will need confirmation that no PHI is stored longer than defined windows and we need deletion proofs for audits.
45:25 Jordan: We'll provide deletion proofs and retention controls available in Dedicated/Private. We'll note them in the security doc.

47:00 Evan: Quick check — can we get a sample billing export format to validate finance integration?
47:07 Jordan: Yes, we'll attach a sample CSV and the API endpoint docs.

48:30 Tomás: Sounds good. I think we have enough to start the pilot planning. Any final clarifications?
48:40 Priya: No, thanks all.
48:43 Leah: Fine from security, awaiting docs.
48:45 Jordan: Great; recap of next steps — Jordan sends runbook and questionnaire answers, Maya sends benchmark plan and network checklist, Leah/Evan provide network diagram and firewall rules. We'll set the security deep dive for next week.
49:10 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the artifacts. End call.

Notes: transcript contains minor auto-caption errors and occasional speaker mislabels; some product names transcribed slightly off (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes as "K V cache"), filler words retained.
